summary: 80-foot Aermotor LS40 tower erected 1950 in Allegany County, NY; closed 1971, sold at auction 1973; now on private land and closed to the public.

access.note: On private land. The NHLR and the NYSFFLA Southern Tier list both say it is closed to the public.

visit.trail_note: Closed to the public on private land; not a place to visit or climb.

events.note: Erected by the state Conservation Department as an 80-foot Aermotor LS40 tower; the observer's cabin date is disputed
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description: the tower top had no observation cabin; the Eastern lookouts site says a cabin was added after 1964
Officially closed at the end of the 1971 season as aerial detection took over
Offered at public auction; the high bidder was the owner of the land where the tower stood
Registered May 22, 2022 as US 1595, NY 47; nominated by Laurie Rankin

notes_for_editor: Core facts agree across NHLR, the NYSFFLA Southern Tier list and the Eastern lookouts site: 1950 Aermotor LS40 erected by the Conservation Department, officially closed 1971, 1973 auction, now on private land and closed to the public. Open items for a human: (1) the observer's cabin date is disputed. The 1941-model cabin is said to date from 1950, but the 1964 survey description quoted by the Eastern site says there was no cabin at the top and that one was added later; the story reports both and does not pick a side. (2) Record coordinates (FFLA 42.04976, -78.01363) and NHLR (42.054757, -78.014137) are 557 m apart, as the record's own conflict note says; no source here settles which point is the tower. (3) The 80 ft figure is overall height; the sources do not give height to the cab floor, so height_m is left unset. (4) The record's agency 'Private Owner' matches NHLR; the Conservation Department built the tower but is not the current administrator. (5) The current landowner is a private individual and is deliberately not named. (6) Visit or access after 2002 is not documented; access is recorded as private/closed on the strength of NHLR and NYSFFLA.
